PullRequest.Title: agentHost: expand E2E workspace and lifecycle coverage
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Expand meaningful bundled-provider E2E coverage without changing production behavior:
- Multi-root peer folder scoping, runtime working-directory execution, restart persistence, delegated folders, and additional worktree ownership/cleanup.
- Automation cancellation, durable failed runs, request deduplication, and new-run definition updates across providers.
- Synchronized input draft clearing, explicit answer replacement, cancellation, and follow-up turns.
- Real Git checkout safety: dirty-worktree errors, stash/commit preservation, index-lock recovery, and deleted target branches.
- MCP application side channels through real Copilot/Codex runtimes: tool schemas, structured arguments, concurrent clients, binary/HTML resources, errors, and stop/start.
- Ignored-file worktree copying with partial/overlapping globs, tracked-path collisions, binary files, archive persistence, and missing-checkout cleanup.
- Provider-backed Git checkpoint comparisons, staged-index preservation, historical content reads, and restart.
- Copilot conversation compaction and cross-provider model API error classification, retries, and recovery.

Preserve newly exposed product gaps as narrowly gated repros with user-facing explanations in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`. No assertions are weakened to accept those failures.

## Coverage

**66 new scenario declarations across two rounds**, yielding **106 additional passing executions**. The continuation adds 37 declarations / 66 passing executions, rather than treating the first green batch as the end of the coverage effort. Provider-scoped gaps are documented in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`. Added 82 model captures and re-recorded four existing MCP captures for deterministic startup readiness.

| Metric | Fresh baseline | Final | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lines/statements | 117,969 / 160,837 (73.34%) | 119,113 / 160,837 (74.05%) | +1,144 covered, +0.71pp |
| Branches | 15,968 / 23,191 (68.85%) | 16,635 / 23,886 (69.64%) | +667 covered, +0.79pp |
| Functions | 4,608 / 6,735 (68.41%) | 4,672 / 6,739 (69.32%) | +64 covered, +0.91pp |
| Local passing / expected-pending | 727 / 91 | 833 / 109 | +106 passing, +18 gated executions |

The +10-percentage-point stretch goal is **not reached**. The continuation's own fresh baseline was 118,386 lines (73.60%); it adds **727 covered lines / +0.45pp**, with +317 covered branches and +32 covered functions. These measurements were collected before merging newer main at `26427d0cb55`, so they do not attribute upstream additions to this work. Native V8 branch/function denominators and asynchronous executable ranges vary between runs.

Notable continuation line gains: Git service 75.71% -> 85.39%, shared proxy error mapping 71.55% -> 91.37%, Codex MCP inventory 79.31% -> 89.19%, and CopilotAgentSession +156 covered lines. The first round also lifted checkout operation handling 31.09% -> 88.23% and additional worktrees 36.84% -> 80.00%.

## Stability work

- Preserve persistence for intentional within-test restarts, but rotate provider homes before subsequent tests and routine recycling; this prevents discovered native conversations from contaminating later catalog and snapshot tests.
- Wait for asynchronous process-log creation before checking exported debug manifests.
- Materialize the default chat and wait for MCP `Ready` before captured calls in the four existing runtime MCP scenarios; retain real tool-result and filesystem assertions.
- Strengthen runtime-directory oracles to use relative shell commands without `cwd`/`workdir` overrides, assert intermediate synchronized input drafts, and pin checkout repository line endings.
- Preserve recorded retry-control headers; a unit round-trip test verifies behavior-affecting headers survive while unrelated/volatile response headers do not.
- Resolve review findings by staging user files before the baseline checkpoint and asserting an ignored execution witness for edit-and-restore tests.
- Defer workspace cleanup until the shared provider lease exits, avoiding Windows MCP subprocess directory locks. Keep the Windows compacted-history persistence defect narrowly gated; macOS/Linux request matching remains strict.

## Validation

- Complete strict replay coverage run: **833 passing / 109 expected pending**. Local runs use `AGENT_HOST_E2E_JOBS=1` to reduce contention on the shared development machine; no timeouts or assertions were loosened.
- Continuation scenarios validated in focused strict replay; retry-header unit suite: **3 passing**.
- Typecheck, targeted hygiene, layering, diff checks, fixture normalization review, and independent stability review passed; review findings addressed.
- A representative conformance scenario also passed in recording mode without creating a per-test capture.
- Merged current main without rewriting branch history. Full post-merge and post-cleanup replay passed: **833 passing / 109 expected pending**, using the runner's standard CI timing settings on the shared development machine.
- [Current Code OSS workflow](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36076192701) is **green**, including Windows, Linux, and macOS integration.
- Continuation repeat builds [477035](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477035) and [477036](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477036) passed all four E2E entrypoints on every platform, including **65 new passing executions on Windows and 66 each on Linux/macOS: 394 new-case successes**. Their separate macOS Codex permissions failures were subsequently fixed by porting the exact fixture-root change from #337826: CI-owned temp roots avoid Codex's intentional allowance for macOS system scratch directories.
- Final [ADO build 477111](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=477111) **succeeded**, including Windows, Linux, and macOS Electron integration. Its macOS log confirms all six formerly failing permission cases pass. Targeted local validation of the eight permission tests plus the corrected checkout title also passed (9 tests).
- The first-round Code OSS workflow and two three-platform ADO builds passed before this continuation.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The ownership path is explicit: all suite fixtures append to one tempDirs array, the diff removes its after-each drain, and the remaining drain is only suiteTeardown. Exact byte magnitude depends on provider and platform, but suite-lifetime retention and serial final deletion are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Temporary workspace directories, Git repositories/worktrees, and their filesystem bytes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Peak retained disk and final cleanup work now grow with every tempDirs.push across the entire suite; the suite has dozens of allocation sites and hundreds of executions, whereas the existing shared host is already recycled every 40 tests.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased peak disk usage and a large serial filesystem-deletion tail at suite teardown, with risk of CI disk pressure or teardown timeouts on slower Windows filesystems.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: After each test released its sessions, teardown called removeTempDirs(tempDirs), which spliced and synchronously deleted all workspaces created by that test before the next test ran.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The diff removes per-test removal and leaves tempDirs populated until suiteTeardown, even though the provider process is stopped and restarted periodically by the lease.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The deleted LEFT-side line `await removeTempDirs(tempDirs);` at old line 148 removes the per-test cleanup boundary; the added comment explicitly defers these resources until suite teardown.
Findings.Title: Bound deferred workspace cleanup to each server generation
Findings.Impact: A normal full Agent Host E2E run now retains every test repository/worktree until the provider suite ends. As the expanded suite runs, CI workers accumulate all workspace bytes and then must delete the complete backlog on the suite's 120-second teardown critical path.
Findings.Evidence: The deleted call was the only per-test consumer of tempDirs; suiteTeardown still calls removeTempDirs only after lease.dispose. removeTempDirs performs recursive rmSync for each queued path. The harness caps a shared server generation at MAX_TESTS_PER_SHARED_SERVER = 40 and _recycleSharedServer stops that process, but it has no hook to drain tempDirs, so retention continues across safe cleanup boundaries. Repository search shows numerous tempDirs.push sites, including Git workspaces and .worktrees directories, and this PR adds more in the new suites.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the Windows handle-safety intent, but drain pending test directories whenever the lease actually stops/recycles the provider (and at final teardown), or attempt immediate deletion and defer only locked paths. This bounds retention to at most one shared-server generation instead of the full suite.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The retry multiplicity and collector call path are explicit. The exact number of duplicate artifacts varies with logger startup timing and log size, which lowers severity but not confidence in the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem scans/copies, ZIP compression CPU, and retained debug-artifact bytes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is O(current log bytes × readiness attempts): retry can invoke collection 100 times at 50 ms intervals, and the shared server's logs grow over earlier tests.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Extra E2E latency, CPU/I/O pressure, and temporary disk growth on CI when process-log creation lags initialization.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each affected test invoked collectDebugLogs once, producing one copied directory or ZIP artifact.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: collectPopulatedDebugLogs now retries the full collectDebugLogs operation until the manifest contains the asynchronously created process log.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT-side line `const artifact = await collectDebugLogs(kind);` is inside `retry(..., 50, 100)`, moving full artifact creation into the readiness-poll loop.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding the full debug artifact while polling readiness
Findings.Impact: When the asynchronous logger is late, the archive test repeatedly recopies and recompresses all host/provider logs, while the directory test repeatedly copies them. Failed-poll artifacts remain leased for ten minutes, so a slow CI worker can retain many duplicate log sets before the test proceeds.
Findings.Evidence: collectDebugLogs crosses AHP into AgentHostDebugLogsCollector.collect. Every call creates a staging directory, asks each provider to copy diagnostics, copies Agent Host logs, stats every file, and for `archive` calls zip(). Successful artifacts are scheduled for cleanup only after the 10-minute lease. The new retry repeats that complete path up to 100 times solely to observe one file's arrival.
Findings.Recommendation: Poll a cheap readiness signal for the process log first, then call collectDebugLogs once. If no direct signal is available, use a slower/backed-off probe and explicitly remove each rejected artifact before retrying, reserving ZIP creation for the final successful collection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Per-test Agent Host E2E acquisition, session release, workspace cleanup, and shared-server recycling
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each test must acquire/connect before execution and release/dispose its sessions afterward; workspace deletion was previously on that per-test teardown path but is now deferred to suiteTeardown after lease disposal. Final suite completion blocks on recursive deletion of the accumulated backlog.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch session/chat state, dispose claimed terminals, and dispose each created session over AHP
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Sequentially once per created session, plus terminal disposals; usually one session but some scenarios create peers or automations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session cleanup ran before each test workspace was deleted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks per-test release before the next test can safely reuse the shared host.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop and relaunch the Agent Host/provider process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per 40 tests or 25 model-backed tests, and around explicit restart scenarios.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Explicit within-test restart did not force an additional post-test fresh data directory; routine recycling did not rotate provider homes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks acquisition/release at generation boundaries; explicit restart tests also force a fresh generation afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursive synchronous deletion of queued test workspaces, Git repositories, and worktrees
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously drained after each test; now one suite-final pass over every path pushed by all tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: removeTempDirs(tempDirs) ran after every test and bounded retained fixtures to that test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removed from each test but moved onto the suite-final critical path, while all bytes remain live until then.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tests and tempDirs.push calls, including repositories and .worktrees; the PR adds over one hundred executions and several new allocation sites.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session cleanup and rmSync deletion are serialized. Shared host reuse is capped at 40 tests, but deferred directories are not drained when that process stops.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Replay mode keeps a warm host/provider SDK client within a generation. Restarts and routine rotation create fresh home/user-data directories; no cache or coalescing bounds the separate tempDirs backlog.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff deletes the sole per-test drain, the shared array has many producers, and only suiteTeardown remains.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact disk bytes and deletion duration depend on provider, platform, and fixture contents, but suite-wide retention versus per-test deletion is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cleanup-lifecycle regression: defer locked workspaces only until a provider stop/recycle, not for the full suite.

Scenarios.Scenario: Host-wide debug archive and directory E2E scenarios waiting for asynchronous process-log creation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test cannot inspect or stream its expected artifact until collectPopulatedDebugLogs returns a manifest containing the process log.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per retry attempt, up to 100 attempts at 50 ms intervals for each of two tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each test issued one collection call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every attempt is awaited serially before the readiness assertion and next delay.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create staging, copy provider and Agent Host logs, enumerate/stat files, and retain a directory artifact
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One complete copy per retry attempt for directory collection; rejected artifacts remain leased for ten minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All copies are on the retry critical path and duplicate current log bytes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: ZIP the complete staged log set for archive collection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One ZIP build per archive readiness attempt, up to 100.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Compression and resulting file creation complete before the retry can inspect entries.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Logger startup delay divided by attempt duration/50 ms, multiplied by the current shared-server log volume.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Attempts are fully serialized; no coalescing or reuse occurs between artifacts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No artifact cache is reused. Every attempt generates a UUID and new files; successful but rejected artifacts have a ten-minute cleanup lease.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the retry directly encloses full collection, and the collector implementation proves copy, stat, ZIP, and lease behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Logger lag is usually short but was observed often enough to motivate the retry; accumulated log size depends on test order and provider trace verbosity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression; readiness should be checked cheaply before materializing the final artifact.

Scenarios.Scenario: New MCP side-channel coverage through real provider-backed stdio servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each scenario creates a session, performs one replayed no-tool model turn to materialize the default chat, waits for MCP Ready, then sends direct AHP tool/resource calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch a Node MCP stdio server for the session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One server per scenario; tests are separate and session cleanup owns shutdown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These scenarios and their subprocesses did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Server readiness blocks every scenario before its assertion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serve one recorded model request through the local replay proxy
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one warm-up turn per scenario; side-channel calls assert no additional model request where relevant.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The warm-up is on setup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: AHP tools/list, tools/call, resource inventory/read, stop/start, and second-client calls
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A small fixed count per scenario; the concurrency case issues three tool calls together.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Calls are the behavior under test; Promise.all creates only a bounded burst of three.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed scenario count and fixed tool/resource payloads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tests run under the existing runner limits; only the explicit three-call scenario is concurrent. There is no input-sized fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The shared host can be warm, but each session gets a new MCP process. Replay fixtures are loaded per test and no model calls occur after warm-up for side-channel operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider process startup duration varies, but cardinality is fixed and intentional coverage cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: all new subprocess/IPC work is bounded test coverage and does not change production execution paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Provider checkpoint, checkout, detached-worktree, and workspace delegation coverage
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tests construct small repositories, execute provider turns or AHP operations, run Git comparisons/worktree lifecycle commands, and verify filesystem state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed handful per scenario over tiny fixture repositories; sibling delegation creates at most two worktrees.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The newly declared scenarios did not execute these boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous setup commands and awaited host operations block each test by design.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/edit/read fixture files, copy selected ignored files, archive/unarchive checkouts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Small fixed file sets except include-file behavior, whose test fixtures are deliberately tiny.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly on scenario setup and assertions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recorded provider turns for shell edits, workspace delegation, and restart persistence
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Fixed turns per scenario; checkpoint edit helper adds one settling turn after each edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each turn serializes before checkpoint comparison or restart.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed test fixture file counts, two sibling worktrees at most, and a fixed number of turns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Git and provider turns are serialized; no collection-sized Promise.all or subprocess burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider host may be warm between tests; explicit restart scenarios preserve state within the test then rotate afterward. Git operations use isolated repositories with auto-GC disabled.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Platform-specific Git latency varies, but work is fixed and test-only.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the suite-wide cleanup retention; per-scenario expensive work is intentional and bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automation, input-draft, compaction, and provider-error/retry lifecycle coverage
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Scenarios create/authenticate sessions, send a bounded sequence of AHP actions and replay-backed model turns, optionally restart the host, then subscribe for terminal state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: HTTP model requests to the local CAPI replay proxy, including injected retry responses
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Fixed per test; retry scenarios require at least two requests only for provider/status combinations designed to retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These model-backed scenarios did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited provider turns block assertions; no real external network is used in replay.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: AHP automation run/subscribe/cancel, input synchronization, session/chat subscribe, and restart recovery calls
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Small fixed sequences; polling is bounded and per single run/channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Calls serialize lifecycle state transitions needed by each test.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist automation/session/provider homes across explicit restart and create isolated workspaces
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One workspace per scenario and one preserved home within restart tests; a fresh home is selected afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Intentional restart did not force post-test home rotation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Host restart blocks the affected tests and post-test release.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed scenarios, one run/session in most cases, and bounded provider retries encoded by fixtures.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Lifecycle calls and turns are mostly sequential. Automation polling repeatedly subscribes to one run; no aggregate run burst is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Replay fixtures isolate each test while the host/provider client is reused up to configured generation caps. Error captures preserve behavior-affecting retry headers; no new production cache exists.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider startup/retry latency differs by platform, but cardinality is bounded and intentional.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: added workload is explicit coverage, not a changed product hot path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full 107-file inventory, executable diffs, modified captures, harness lifecycle, and transitive subprocess/IPC/filesystem boundaries. Reported two diff-caused test-infrastructure regressions: suite-wide temporary workspace retention after removal of per-test cleanup, and repeated full debug-artifact construction inside a readiness poll. No production runtime path was changed, and the remaining added E2E subprocess, Git, replay-network, and IPC work is bounded by fixed scenarios.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
